articleTitle: Modulation as a basis for calculating the balanced and unbalanced magnetic forces in rotating field electrical machines
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Mechanical and electromagnetic irregularities such as stationary and rotating eccentricities are resolved into modulation functions which are applied to an ideal machine excited with a balanced supply. This procedure yields expressions for the unbalanced magnetic pull and vibrational force.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: On 27 September last year, a gaily painted, streamlined train slid silently into Geneva's Cornavin Railway Station. It was the long-awaited ‘Train à Grande Vitesse’ (High Speed Train) of the French National Railways (SNCF), linking Geneva to Paris in 4 h and 20 min as opposed to 6 h in the pre-TG V era.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: To suspend the rotor of a magnetic bearing a positional control system is required. A suitable compensator it developed by the state-variable feedback technique. The resulting compensator design is verified by simulation of the non-linear system. The compensator was also practically tested on the physical system and the system functioned well with the aid of the compensators.

articleTitle: Synchronous machine saturation models in the presence of a voltage regulator
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper offers a further contribution to the evaluation of several simple mathematical models which represent magnetic saturation in a synchronous machine. Particular attention it paid to quadrature axis saturation in conjunction with an automatic voltage regulator and either a slow electro-magnetic exciter or a fast thyristor exciter. Calculated transient response results are compared in order to evaluate both the accuracy and computational economy of each saturation model.

articleTitle: Prediction of impurity distribution for ion implanted boron into silicon at high energies for the manufacture of high speed bipolar transistors
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The contribution investigates possibilities for predicting distributions of boron as dopant after implantation into silicon. The existing work for range predictions up to implantation energies of 1 000 keV if corrected and extended to allow computer calculation of the distributions up to 1 500 keV. Possibility of application to the manufacture of high speed bipolar transistors is pointed out.

articleTitle: Reduction of energy losses in magnetic bearings due to imbalance signals
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Cyclic displacement signals arising from rotor imbalance give rise to unnecessary losses in actively controlled magnetic bearing). A discrete notch filter that tracks the rotor rotation frequency may be used to eliminate these imbalance signals. Alternately the total displacement signal is sampled in such away that the imbalance signal component is aliased to appear as a dc component. In both cases the associated losses are eliminated.

articleTitle: Item of practical interest: Determination of the apparent movement of the sun
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: As a preliminary to the description of a simple piece of apparatus, possibly novel in character, for determining the apparent paths of the sun at the summer and winter solstices leading to the development of a new type of solar heater, reference is made to generally well-known facts relating to the daily and annual motion of the earth as depicted respectively in Fig 1, Fig 2 and Fig 3. As an example, Pretoria is taken as the place of observation of the sun's apparent motion.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A statistical method is presented for application to simple voltage magnitude measurements in a three phase system to yield values for the voltage phases in magnitude and displacement to a very high degree of accuracy.

articleTitle: The electrification of greater Soweto: its socio-economic impact
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Greater Soweto consists of considerably more than 1-million people living in three municipal areas governed by three community councils. Before examining the details of the existing area however, it would be of interest to briefly trace the historical background to the creation of Greater Soweto.

articleTitle: The drakensberg pumped storage scheme: Description of scheme and principal data
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper contains a description of the Drakensberg Pumped Storage Scheme as a whole, its functions, main features of the upper and lower reservoirs, the geometry and dimensions of the waterways, arrangement of underground caverns as well as the principal hydro-mechanical data of the scheme. Certain aspects of the philosophy adopted in the design of the scheme are also presented in the paper.

articleTitle: The earthing of the neutral in low voltage distribution systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In 1980, a Code of Practice for the multiple earthing of the neutral of a low voltage reticulation system was drafted by the City Electrical Engineer's Department of the City of Johannesburg. The object was to formulate the safety aspects of the various systems in use, i.e. PME (Protective Multiple Earthing) and MEN (Multiple Earthed Neutral) and to clarify the difference between the two systems and their relative merits.

articleTitle: Electrical aspects of the Drakensberg pumpedstorage plant
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper is a concise description of the equipment installed at Drakensberg Pumped Storage Scheme as well as some of the considerations which influenced the choice of equipment used. In particular the operation of a modern pumped storage scheme places severe demands upon the equipment which must be designed to provide a greater than normal, degree of reliability. Considerations of starting methods are given as well as the criteria under which electrical stability is maintained. A brief outline of electrical protection is also provided. The emergency systems are described together with the philosophy which leads to their use. A brief description of the generator transformer is provided.

articleTitle: Aspects of the control room design
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes the control system at a pump storage scheme and highlights some of the differences between this system and the controls at conventional power stations. it also describes a custom-built Vectormeter which, as far as we know, is a world-first.

articleTitle: The role of the electrical engineer in a regional water authority such as the Rand water board
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Since the time of the discovery of gold on the Witwatersrand water has played an important part in the development of this region and indeed is probably the most important single resource on which this whole metropolis depends. The location of the Witwatersrand some 350 m above and 50 km from the nearest major source of water, the Vaal River, makes it unique and creates special problems for the water supply authority which are not encountered in most other parts of the world.

articleTitle: Lightning overvoltage protection of the drakensberg 420 kV SF6 gas-insulated substation
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The 420 kV SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> gas-insulated, metalclad switchgear installation for the Drakensberg pumped storage plant serves as a practical example of the factors to be considered in substation lightning overvoltage protection, e.g. against distant or close-in lightning strokes, whether lightning strikes a phase conductor of the overhead transmission line or the tower/earthwire. By carefully selecting and positioning the surge arresters and by taking suitable precautionary measures on the overhead line side, an extensive installation such as Drakensberg can be safely and economically protected against lightning overvoltages.

articleTitle: Sintese van aktiewe en passiewe resistor-termistor temperatuurkompensasie stroombane
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The contribution indicates the analogy between resistor-thermistor circuits and resistor-capacitor circuits. Methods for the synthesis of passive and active resistor-thermistor circuits ire developed from this analogy. It if also proven that a passive temperature compensating circuit can always be synthesized in the form of a ladder network when a suitable dc offset voltage is added to the prescribed transfer function.

abstract: An investigation into the technology of VMOS power transistors was undertaken. A first order model for determining the relationship between the physical characteristics and the electrical parameters was developed and implemented in a computer program. Etching of V-grooves and processing of non-planar surfaces were investigated. A VMOS power transistor was designed and manufactured.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents an overview of current earthing practice in the Republic of South Africa and points out various deficiencies in current practice. It further identifies some of the technical causes underlying these deficiencies. The emphasis lies on examples and practical test results.

articleTitle: A technique for assessing space harmonic effects in squirrel cage induction motors
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper describes the production of harmonic fields in induction motors and their influence on the torque-speed curve. A technique it developed for assessing the merits of slot combinations and winding arrangements with regard to the production of harmonic asynchronous and synchronous torques. The method is applied to a number of motors and the validity of the assessments made are checked by examining the measured torque-speed curves of these machines.

articleTitle: The use of aluminium conductors in transformers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In a wide range of electrical applications the use of aluminium instead of copper has increased considerably during the last decades. The reasons that have led to this development specifically with regard to transformer design and the technical advantages arising thereof are discussed.

articleTitle: Errors in the measurement of the complex components of apparent power
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The errors which occur due to volt and current transformers, used in three phase-three and four wire power end VAr measurements are analysed, taking into Account the volt and current transformation errors, supply volt, load unbalance and load power factor. It it shown that a certain choice of VT ratio leads to acceptably low errors in measurement, irrespective of the accuracy class of the volt and current transformer. It is also shown that the three phase-four wire VAr measurement has a considerably lower error than its three phase-three wire counterpart.

articleTitle: Nuclear power: An emerging answer to energy and economic problems thirtieth bernard price memorial lecture
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The potential for nuclear power to contribute to energy solutions is strong. With this contribution, the pressures on economic, social and political problems may be eased so that the benefits, of nuclear power will have a ripple effect. Important questions need to be addressed in the decade ahead, including questions related to assurances of health and safety to the public, the effective management of nuclear - wastes, and the continued use of nuclear power solely for peaceful purposes rather than as a channel for nuclear weapons proliferation. Effective solutions to these problems will permit the deployment of breeder reactors, advanced thermal reactors, and fusion reactors. Ultimately, the social and political structure of the world must rest, not on finite sources of energy, but on these and other renewable energy resources.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: It is a very long time since I addressed a gathering of electrical engineers in this hall, and I must say that I experience pangs of nostalgia when thinking of the many memorable meetings that I attended here and the many enjoyable functions that my wife and I took part in. So when I was asked to speak to you this afternoon, I jumped at the opportunity of renewing old friendships and associations, always tinged with the sorrow that so many of them were with people who have now passed away. Although my address to you is by no means intended to be a service in memoriam, it is inevitable that if I am to talk about the growth of electrical engineering in South Africa I should be thinking about the men we knew who promoted and fostered its growth. However, the letter inviting me to speak at this function suggested an address ‘of a light-hearted nature’, and so I will content myself with remembering our many friends and associates of the past and believing that in spirit they are with us in this significant year of the 150th anniversary of Michael Faraday and Joseph Henry.

articleTitle: The drakensberg project: Water and power for South Africa
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper outlines the planning of The Tugela-Vaal Scheme and, particularly the Drakensberg Project — a major undertaking combining an 11 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/s inter-burn water transfer with a 1 000 MW pumped storage hydro-electric installation. It describes how co-operation between the authorities responsible for water and electricity supply resulted in a cost saving to the country of R50 million (March 1979 values). It also sets out the basis of this joint participation in the financing and construction of the scheme. Finally, there is a glimpse of possible future extensions.

articleTitle: Power system aspects of pumped storage plant
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In a pumped storage installation electrical power is generated at times of system peak load by allowing water from an upper reservoir to flow through a turbine/generator to a lower reservoir. At times of light load this water is pumped back from the lower to the upper reservoir, generally using the generator as a motor and the turbine as a pump. The pumping energy is supplied by generating plant on the system which would otherwise be shut down or operated at low output at times of light load.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Insulation co-ordination implies the selection of the electric insulation characteristics of equipment with regard to its application and in relation to its surroundings. Consideration must be given to the voltages which can appear within the system, to the location and characteristics of the overvoltage protective devices, to the continuity of service desired and to the safety of persons and property, so that the probability of undesired incidents due to voltage stresses is reduced to ensure an economically and operationally acceptable performance. In recent years, the IEC set up Sub-Committee 28A: Insulation Co-ordination for Low-voltage Equipment, to establish an international system for insulation co-ordination within low-voltage systems. This would eliminate present problems caused through existing standards which specify diverse design criteria for dimensions of clearances and creepage distances. For equipment, it would also enable designers to specify insulation performance criteria for electrical equipment and installations and systems which are becoming more complex. SC 28A was assigned a ‘safety pilot function’, which meant that its recommendations would be taken into consideration by other Technical and Sub-Committees when specifying creepage and clearance distance requirements for products for which they are responsible.

articleTitle: Wide scope of IEC work on electromagnetic compatibility problems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Systematic study of man-made radio noise and interference phenomena began in the period between 1920 and 1940, when radio broadcasting was becoming commonplace and governments world-wide found it necessary to regulate this expanding communication technique. This applied not only to general broadcasting, but to point-to-point communication, it being evident that the radio spectrum was limited and that unless regulated, various kinds of interference phenomena could occur. With regulation, although interference occurs occasionally, communications can generally be accomplished, both reliably and relatively inexpensively. Summary Although the various Technical Committees and Sub-Committees have particular interests in certain aspects of emc, there is much common science basic to those interests. Recognizing this, the Committee of Action approved the formation of the Committee of Action Emc Co-ordinating Working Group. (Its formal structure was approved in June 1980 with permanent members being representatives from TCs or SCs 12, 17B, 18, 40, 41B, 45A, 62, 65, 77 and CISPR. (Other representatives may join as is deemed advisable from time to time.) Its function is to give guidance to the various TCs, SCs and WGs concerned with emc to develop most expeditiously the minimum number of standard techniques and procedures required by the IEC. It is agreed that, most likely, particular immunity requirements must be decided by the individual product committees. However, not only individual committees such as TC 77 and CISPR, but also other committees should take the initiative in developing test methods and codes of practice which may have general application.

articleTitle: Dynamic behaviour of a multi-induction motor system
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper presents a method of analysing induction motor dynamic behaviour in a multimotor system. This investigation, unlike previous ones, represents the motors as well as the distribution network elements in terms of their two-axis equations in order to illustrate the effect of using different mathematical models for the motors especially when they are supplied by series capacitor compensated feeders. The results show that the simplified models of the motors do not ‘fail-to-safety’, and that conclusions drawn from a single-machine-infinite-busbar investigation are not necessarily applicable to a multimotor system. A computer program has been developed which allows the user to simply specify the network topology, loads, motors and motor busbars of the system together with the location of any one of four possible disturbances. The program then automatically configures the network, sets up all the equations, carries out a load flow solution for steady initial conditions, and calculates the transient response. The size of the multimotor system to be investigated is limited only by the size and accuracy of the computer.

articleTitle: Environmental impact control — new technology or new philosophy?
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: After the historical development of engineering has been outlined to arrive at the concept of ‘environmental design’, the chaos currently present in some countries is discussed briefly in order to define its multiple cause. Subsequently the multiple solution to the problem is indicated, stressing that it has mainly a philosophical character, without which the process of environmental impact control, which is also discussed in general, cannot be executed effectively. It is explained that the appropriate philosophy centres around the proper definition of ‘environment’, and that the issue at stake is really the maintenance of balance between nature conservation and cultural development. Finally, the matrix and mapping techniques for documenting data in the environmental impact analysis process are discussed briefly.
